content: 1. Hamilton RG discussed the epidemiology, clinical manifestations, and diagnostic approaches to latex allergy in a comprehensive review published on the UpToDate website between 2014 and 2016. 2. Casanova LM and colleagues conducted a study assessing the risk of self-contamination during the removal of personal protective equipment (PPE) used in the care of Ebola patients. Their findings were published in the journal Infection Control and Hospital Epidemiology in 2016, highlighting critical infection control practices. 3. Houlihan CF et al. performed a cross-sectional study examining Ebola exposure, illness experiences, and antibody prevalence among international responders to the West African Ebola epidemic (2014–2016). The results were published in PLOS Medicine in 2017. 4. Reidy P and collaborators developed and evaluated a PPE solution tailored for UK military medical personnel working in Ebola treatment units in Sierra Leone. Their findings were published in Journal of Hospital Infection in 2017. 5. Cummings KJ and colleagues addressed infection prevention and control strategies in the first U.S. community hospital to care for Ebola patients. Their work, published in Annals of Internal Medicine in 2016, provided a framework for national recommendations and future strategies. 6. Mehtar S et al. investigated the deliberate exposure of humans to chlorine as a consequence of the Ebola outbreak in West Africa. Their study, published in Antimicrobial Resistance and Infection Control in 2016, explored the aftermath of such practices. 7. The World Health Organization (WHO) published comprehensive guidelines on hand hygiene in healthcare settings in 2009, emphasizing its critical role in infection prevention. 8. Casanova LM and colleagues assessed viral transfer risks during the doffing of Ebola-level PPE in a biocontainment unit. Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2018. 9. Olu O and collaborators conducted a retrospective descriptive study on the epidemiology of Ebola virus transmission among healthcare workers in Sierra Leone from May to December 2014. The study was published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2015. 10. Savini H et al. examined occupational exposures to the Ebola virus in an Ebola treatment center in Conakry, Guinea. Their findings were published in Emerging Infectious Diseases in 2017. 11. Jacobs M and colleagues reported on the use of experimental antiviral agents for post-exposure prophylaxis against Ebola virus disease in healthcare workers. This case series was published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2015. 12. Hoff NA and collaborators conducted a seroprevalence study of Ebola virus among healthcare workers in the Yambuku Health Zone, Democratic Republic of Congo. Their findings were published in The American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2017. 13. Doshi RH et al. identified risk factors for Ebola exposure among healthcare workers in Boende, Tshuapa Province, Democratic Republic of Congo. Their study was published in The Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2020. 14. Gsell P-S and colleagues reported on the operational and safety outcomes of ring vaccination with rVSV-ZEBOV during the 2016 Ebola outbreak in Guinea. Their findings were published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2017. 15. Dunn AC et al. investigated nosocomial transmission of Ebola virus disease in pediatric and maternity wards in Sierra Leone in 2014. Their study was published in American Journal of Infection Control in 2016. 16. Matanoch A and collaborators analyzed Ebola virus disease cases among healthcare workers not working in Ebola treatment units in Liberia between June and August 2014. Their findings were published in 2014. 17. Cook BWM et al. evaluated the disinfection characteristics of various Ebola virus outbreak variants. Their study was published in Scientific Reports in 2016. 18. Schuit M and colleagues compared the stability of Ebola virus Makona-C05 and Yambuku-Maying in blood samples. Their findings were published in PLOS One in 2016. 19. Bibby K et al. investigated the disinfection of Ebola virus in sterilized municipal wastewater. Their study was published in PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2017. 20. Youkee D and collaborators assessed environmental contamination and decontamination practices within an Ebola holding unit in Freetown, Sierra Leone. Their findings were published in PLOS One in 2015. 21. Bausch DG et al. evaluated the risk of Ebola virus transmission from bodily fluids and fomites. Their study was published in The Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2007. 22. Puro V and colleagues examined the persistence of Ebola virus on surfaces after cleaning procedures in high-level isolation settings. Their findings were published in Infection Control and Hospital Epidemiology in 2016. 23. Palich R et al. detected Ebola virus RNA on fomites in close proximity to confirmed Ebola patients in Guinea in 2015. Their study was published in PLOS One in 2017. 24. Wu X et al. investigated environmental contamination with Ebola virus in a convalescent ward. Their findings were published in The Journal of Hospital Infection in 2015. 25. Gallandat K et al. assessed the efficacy of chlorine-based surface disinfection methods using Escherichia coli and an Ebola surrogate. Their findings were published in Environmental Science & Technology in 2018. 26. Smither SJ and colleagues evaluated the effectiveness of various disinfectants against Ebola virus on different materials. Their study was published in Emerging Infectious Diseases in 2018. 27. The World Health Organization published guidelines on the safe management of healthcare waste, including infectious and sharp waste, in 2017. 28. Dietz PM et al. analyzed the epidemiology and risk factors for Ebola virus disease in Sierra Leone from May 2014 to January 2015. Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2015. 29. The International Ebola Response Team conducted a retrospective observational study on exposure patterns driving Ebola transmission in West Africa. Their findings were published in PLOS Medicine in 2016. 30. Senga M et al. identified factors underlying Ebola virus infection among health workers in Kenema, Sierra Leone, during 2014–2015. Their study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2016. 31. Muoghalu IS and collaborators analyzed the transmission chain of the 2014–2015 Ebola virus disease outbreak in Koinadugu District, Sierra Leone. Their findings were published in Frontiers in Public Health in 2017. 32. Tiffany A et al. quantified the impact of safe and dignified burials during the 2013–2016 West African Ebola epidemic. Their study was published in The American Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2016. 33. Lee-Kwan SH et al. explored facilitators and barriers to community acceptance of safe, dignified medical burials during the Ebola epidemic in Sierra Leone in 2014. Their findings were published in Journal of Health Communication in 2017. 34. Caleo G and colleagues investigated factors affecting household transmission dynamics and community compliance with Ebola control measures in a rural village in Sierra Leone. Their study was published in BMC Public Health in 2018. 35. Lyons P et al. engaged religious leaders to promote safe burial practices during the 2014–2016 Ebola outbreak in Sierra Leone. Their findings were published in Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2021. 36. Sikakuly FK et al. examined the socio-cultural and anthropological implications of safe and dignified burials for Ebola victims in the Eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. Their study was published in One Health in 2021. 37. Gautier L et al. evaluated a community-led prevention strategy to enhance behavioral changes toward Ebola virus disease prevention in Western Côte d'Ivoire. Their findings were published in Global Health Research and Policy in 2017. 38. Ratnayake R et al. reviewed highly targeted spatiotemporal interventions against cholera epidemics from 2000 to 2019. Their findings were published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2021. 39. Dahl BA et al. documented the CDC’s response to the 2014–2016 Ebola epidemic in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone. Their findings were published in MMWR and Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report in 2016. 40. Cooper C et al. analyzed infection prevention and control challenges and successes during the Ebola outbreak in Liberia (2014–2015). Their findings were published in BMC Medicine in 2016.
